recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed; if the FMM warning policy is reintroduced, make and test that change in HL7/kindling rather than in this FHIR source checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-23131 was a Published/Persuasive technical correction asking to fix a misleading ResourceValidator build error: the code rejected resources with warnings unless FMM was 0, but the message said resources could not have FMM >1 if they had warnings.
initial_application: No FHIR repository commit explicitly mentions FHIR-23131. The old in-repo tools/java ResourceValidator carried the misleading message until the FHIR repository migrated the publisher to the external kindling dependency and removed that source file. Kindling later corrected the primary message from FMM >1 to FMM > 0.
additional_context: Current FHIR source uses org.hl7.fhir:kindling version 1.25.5-SNAPSHOT for org.hl7.fhir.tools.publisher.Publisher, so the active validator implementation is outside the core checkout. Current kindling has also commented out the FMM warning requirement checks entirely. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting or clarifying community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No source was changed because the named core file no longer exists, the active build-tool source is external, and that external source has already corrected and then disabled the confusing check.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive technical correction reporting that ResourceValidator enforced an FMM0 rule while saying resources could not have FMM >1 if they had warnings.
